claim: Hearing loss is a widespread public health issue affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide.
source: Hearing loss is a widespread public health issue affecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide.
evidence: This is a general statement about the prevalence of hearing loss, representing established knowledge in the field.

claim: Hearing loss can be treated with cochlear implants or hearing aids but biological restoration of cochlear structure and function is not currently possible.
source: Hearing loss can be treated with cochlear implants or hearing aids but biological restoration of cochlear structure and function is not currently possible.
evidence: This statement reflects current clinical knowledge about treatment options and limitations.

claim: Hearing is mediated by mechanosensitive hair cells in the organ of Corti.
source: Hearing is mediated by mechanosensitive hair cells in the organ of Corti, and loss or damage to these cells results in sensorineural hearing loss.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the mechanism of hearing.

claim: Loss or damage to hair cells results in sensorineural hearing loss.
source: Hearing is mediated by mechanosensitive hair cells in the organ of Corti, and loss or damage to these cells results in sensorineural hearing loss.
evidence: This is established scientific knowledge about the cause of sensorineural hearing loss.

claim: Mammals are capable of very modest spontaneous hair cell regeneration in the balance organs.
source: Although mammals are only capable of very modest spontaneous hair cell regeneration in the balance organs (Bramhall et al., 2014; Cox et al., 2014; Forge et al., 1993; Golub et al., 2012; Kawamoto et al., 2009; Kelley et al., 1995; Ogata et al., 1999; Rubel et al., 1995), the cochlea lack this regenerative capability.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: The mammalian cochlea lacks regenerative capability for hair cells.
source: Although mammals are only capable of very modest spontaneous hair cell regeneration in the balance organs (Bramhall et al., 2014; Cox et al., 2014; Forge et al., 1993; Golub et al., 2012; Kawamoto et al., 2009; Kelley et al., 1995; Ogata et al., 1999; Rubel et al., 1995), the cochlea lack this regenerative capability.
evidence: This claim is supported by the contrast with balance organs and is established knowledge in the field.

claim: Robust turnover of hair cells is seen in the balance organs of many non-mammalian vertebrates.
source: Robust turnover of hair cells is seen in the balance organs of many non-mammalian vertebrates (Corwin, 1981; Jørgensen and Mathiesen, 1988; Lanford et al., 1996; Popper and Hoxter, 1990).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Impressive structural and functional recovery can be achieved in the hearing organs of non-mammalian vertebrates following the killing of hair cells.
source: Impressive structural and functional recovery can also be achieved in the hearing organs of non-mammalian vertebrates following the killing of hair cells (Adler and Raphael, 1996; Baird et al., 2000; Corwin and Cotanche, 1988; Cotanche, 1999; Niemiec et al., 1994; Raphael, 1993; Roberson et al., 2004; Roberson et al., 1996; Ryals and Rubel, 1988).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: In non-mammalian vertebrates, supporting cells lying adjacent to hair cells can re-enter the cell cycle and trans-differentiate to generate new hair cells.
source: In these cases, supporting cells lying adjacent to hair cells can re-enter the cell cycle and trans-differentiate to generate new hair cells.
evidence: This claim describes the mechanism of hair cell regeneration in non-mammalian vertebrates, inferred from the cited studies.

claim: ATOH1 is both necessary and sufficient for hair cell development and survival.
source: The basic helix-loop-helix transcription factor ATOH1 is both necessary and sufficient for hair cell development and survival (Bermingham et al., 1999; Cai et al., 2013; Chonko et al., 2013; Driver et al., 2013; Pan et al., 2012; Woods et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Overexpression of ATOH1 can reprogram non-sensory cells of the inner ear into hair-cell-like cells in vitro.
source: In vitro studies using explants of the mammalian cochlea or inner ear balance organs showed that overexpression of ATOH1 can reprogram non-sensory cells of the inner ear into hair-cell-like cells (Jen et al., 2019; Shou et al., 2003; Zheng and Gao, 2000).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior in vitro research.

claim: Adenoviral expression of Atoh1 in the cochlea of guinea pigs deafened with ototoxic drugs shows a variable and partial restoration of hearing after the lesion.
source: Adenoviral expression of Atoh1 in the cochlea of guinea pigs deafened with ototoxic drugs shows a variable and partial restoration of hearing after the lesion (Izumikawa et al., 2005).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: In vivo studies employing neonatal transgenic mice showed that cells of the greater epithelial ridge (GER) and some supporting cells could be reprogrammed to hair-cell-like cells with the ectopic expression of Atoh1 alone.
source: In vivo studies employing neonatal transgenic mice showed that cells of the greater epithelial ridge (GER) that lie next to the organ of Corti, and some supporting cells could be reprogrammed to hair-cell-like cells with the ectopic expression of Atoh1 alone (Kelly et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior in vivo research.

claim: The hair cell reprogramming ability of ATOH1 declines rapidly with age.
source: However, the hair cell reprogramming ability of ATOH1 declines rapidly with age (Kelly et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2012), suggesting a need for additional transcription factors to promote hair cell reprogramming in older animals.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cochleae with flat epithelium do not respond to ATOH1 over-expression.
source: Moreover, cochleae where the auditory epithelium has degenerated further to state lacking hair cell and supporting cells (known as the flat epithelium; Izumikawa et al., 2008) do not respond to ATOH1 over-expression, further indicating the need for a more complex combinatorial approach.
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and inference about the need for combinatorial approaches.

claim: GFI1 and POU4F3 are two hair-cell-specific transcription factors expressed downstream of ATOH1 during development.
source: GFI1 and POU4F3 are two hair-cell-specific transcription factors expressed downstream of ATOH1 during development that has been implicated in hair cell survival and function (Hertzano et al., 2004; Masuda et al., 2011; Wallis et al., 2003; Xiang et al., 1997; Xiang et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: GFI1 and POU4F3 have been implicated in hair cell survival and function.
source: GFI1 and POU4F3 are two hair-cell-specific transcription factors expressed downstream of ATOH1 during development that has been implicated in hair cell survival and function (Hertzano et al., 2004; Masuda et al., 2011; Wallis et al., 2003; Xiang et al., 1997; Xiang et al., 1998).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to prior research.

claim: Adenoviral delivery of ATOH1 and GFI1 to adult mice in which hair cells were ablated promoted regeneration through supporting cell transdifferentiation at a higher efficiency than ATOH1 alone.
source: Adenoviral delivery of ATOH1 and GFI1 to adult mice in which hair cells were ablated promoted regeneration through supporting cell transdifferentiation at a higher efficiency than ATOH1 alone (Lee et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Transgenic over-expression of combinations of ATOH1, GATA3, and POU4F3 reprogrammed adult supporting cells into hair-cell-like cells with improved efficiency.
source: Similarly, transgenic over-expression of combinations of ATOH1, GATA3, and POU4F3 reprogrammed adult supporting cells into hair-cell-like cells with improved efficiency (Walters et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: A combination of ATOH1, GFI1, and POU4F3 reprogrammed embryonic stem cells and chick otic epithelial cells in vitro to cells that expressed several hair cell genes and showed key hair cell features.
source: A combination of ATOH1, GFI1, and POU4F3 reprogrammed embryonic stem cells and chick otic epithelial cells in vitro to cells that expressed several hair cell genes, and showed key hair cell features (Costa et al., 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Co-overexpression of ATOH1, GFI1, and POU4F3 in vivo can reprogram neonatal Lgr5+ supporting cells into hair-cell-like cells more efficiently than ATOH1 alone.
source: The co-overexpression of these three factors in vivo can also reprogram neonatal Lgr5 +supporting cells into hair-cell-like cells more efficiently than ATOH1 alone (Chen et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The addition of SIX1 to the three factor cocktail (ATOH1, GFI1, POU4F3) was able to reprogram adult mouse tail-tip fibroblasts into hair-cell-like cells.
source: Finally, the addition of SIX1 to the three factor cocktail was able to reprogram adult mouse tail-tip fibroblasts into hair-cell-like cells which have some epigenetic and transcriptional characteristics of hair cells, as well as transduction channel protein expression, and hair-cell-like electrophysiological properties (Menendez et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: The chromatin surrounding hair cell genes becomes progressively less accessible as the ear matures.
source: Recent studies have shown that one reason for the inability of cochlear supporting cells to convert to hair cells is that the chromatin surrounding hair cell genes becomes progressively less accessible as the ear matures (Jen et al., 2019; Tao et al., 2021).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Three transgenic mouse lines were generated in which transcription factor combinations (ATOH1 alone, ATOH1 + GFI1, and ATOH1 + GFI1+POU4F3) were expressed from the ROSA26 locus in a Cre-dependent fashion.
source: We generated three transgenic mouse lines in which the transcription factor combinations were expressed from the ROSA26 locus in a Cre-dependent fashion.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: ATOH1 alone is sufficient to reprogram neonatal non-sensory cells of the greater epithelial ridge into large numbers of hair cell-like cells surrounded by GLAST-positive supporting cell-like cells.
source: We found that ATOH1 alone is sufficient to reprogram neonatal non-sensory cells of the greater epithelial ridge into a mosaic of large numbers of hair cell-like cells that are surrounded by GLAST-positive supporting cell-like cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Reprogrammed hair cells in neonatal mice resembled inner hair cells and possessed stereocilia and some mechanotransduction properties.
source: The reprogrammed hair cells resembled inner hair cells and possessed stereocilia and some mechanotransduction properties.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: At young ages (P1-P8), additional transcription factors (GFI1, POU4F3) do not enhance the number of new hair cells generated by ATOH1.
source: At these young ages, additional transcription factors do not enhance the number of new hair cells generated by ATOH1, nor do they increase the number of hair cells genes expressed in these reprogrammed cells, determined by single-cell RNA-seq.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data including scRNA-seq.

claim: At young ages (P1-P8), additional transcription factors (GFI1, POU4F3) do not increase the number of hair cell genes expressed in reprogrammed cells.
source: At these young ages, additional transcription factors do not enhance the number of new hair cells generated by ATOH1, nor do they increase the number of hair cells genes expressed in these reprogrammed cells, determined by single-cell RNA-seq.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by scRNA-seq data.

claim: After the first postnatal week, the overexpression of GFI1 and POU4F3 is necessary to enhance the hair cell reprogramming ability of ATOH1 in 8-day-old supporting cells.
source: However, we show that after the first postnatal week, the overexpression of GFI1 and POU4F3 is necessary to enhance the hair cell reprogramming ability of ATOH1 in 8-day-old supporting cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Some supporting cell populations remain refractory to reprogramming even with three transcription factors, likely due to Notch signaling from endogenous hair cells.
source: We also show that some supporting cell populations remain refractory to reprogramming even with three transcription factors, likely due to the action of the reprogramming factors being blocked by Notch signaling delivered by the endogenous hair cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data and inference about the mechanism.

claim: Hair cell loci become progressively less accessible in supporting cells and non-sensory cells of the cochlea during the first postnatal week.
source: By simultaneously comparing the transcriptome and chromatin accessibility of cochlear cells at birth and 1 week of age using single-cell multi-omic approaches, we showed that hair cell loci become progressively less accessible in supporting cells and non-sensory cells of the cochlea during the first postnatal week.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by multi-omic data.

claim: Individual transcription factor coding regions were separated by a GSG-T2A self-cleaving peptide sequence to ensure comparable transcription factor expression levels.
source: Individual transcription factor coding regions were separated by a GSG-T2A self-cleaving peptide sequence to ensure comparable transcription factor expression levels (Tang et al., 2009).
evidence: This describes a methodological approach, supported by a citation.

claim: Correct targeting efficiency to the Rosa26 locus of approximately 80% was achieved by co-electroporating targeting vectors with a plasmid expressing Cas9 and a sgRNA targeting the Rosa26 locus.
source: We were able to achieve correct targeting efficiency to the Rosa26 locus of approximately 80% by co-electroporating our targeting vectors with a plasmid expressing Cas9 and a sgRNA targeting the Rosa26 locus between the two homology arms.
evidence: This describes a methodological result from the study.

claim: Expression of the transcription factor proteins was verified by culturing mouse ES cell lines with membrane-permeable TAT-Cre protein, followed by western blotting.
source: We verified the expression of the transcription factor proteins by culturing the mouse ES cell lines used to generate founders for the three targeted mouse lines in the presence of membrane-permeable TAT-Cre protein, followed by western blotting (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This describes a methodological validation, supported by western blot data shown in a figure.

claim: Large numbers of reprogrammed hair cells were present throughout the basal-apical axis of the cochlea, with an average of 300 reprogrammed hair cells per 200 μm.
source: Reprogrammed hair cells were present in similar numbers throughout the basal-apical axis of the cochlea, with an average of 300 reprogrammed hair cells per 200 μm, compared to an average of 28 inner hair cells and 90 outer hair cells in a corresponding 200 μm length of the organ of Corti.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: No significant differences in reprogrammed hair cell numbers were observed between the three transcription factor combinations at P8.
source: We did not observe significant differences in reprogrammed hair cell numbers between the three transcription factor combinations at this age (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by quantitative data shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The reprogrammed cells in the GER expressed VGLUT3, a vesicular transport protein expressed in inner hair cells.
source: The reprogrammed cells in the GER expressed VGLUT3, a known vesicular transport protein expressed in inner hair cells (Obholzer et al., 2008; Ruel et al., 2008; Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data and citations.

claim: The reprogrammed cells did not express Prestin, a motor protein specific to outer hair cells.
source: The reprogrammed cells did not express Prestin, a motor protein specific to outer hair cells which is necessary for their electromotility and their contribution to cochlear amplification and tuning (Zheng et al., 2000).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data and a citation.

claim: The reprogrammed hair-cell-like cells in the GER received innervation from auditory afferents.
source: The reprogrammed hair-cell-like cells in the GER received innervation from auditory afferents, labeled with the TuJ1 antibody to βIII-tubulin.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: The hair-cell-like cells stained with antibodies to CTBP2/Ribeye, a major component of ribbon synapses formed between afferent neurons and hair cells.
source: The hair-cell-like cells also stained with antibodies to the CTBP2 transcription factor, which also recognizes Ribeye, a major component of ribbon synapses formed between afferent neurons and hair cells (Sheets et al., 2011).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data and a citation.

claim: Reprogrammed hair cells in the GER had stereocilia-like protrusions with a staircase-like arrangement similar to control hair cells.
source: Under all three reprogramming conditions, reprogrammed hair cells throughout the GER had stereocilia-like protrusions from their apical surfaces, possessing a staircase-like arrangement of hair bundles that appeared similar to control hair cells of the same age (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by scanning electron microscopy data.

claim: Reprogrammed hair cells in the GER took up FM 1-43 dye within 10 seconds, indicating mechanotransduction channel activity.
source: Reprogrammed hair cells in the GER in all three conditions took up the FM 1–43 dye within 10 s (Figure 2B), although the degree of labeling of the reprogrammed cells in the GER was significantly fainter than the endogenous hair cells visible in the organ of Corti.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by FM1-43 dye uptake assay data.

claim: The degree of FM1-43 labeling of reprogrammed cells in the GER was significantly fainter than endogenous hair cells.
source: Reprogrammed hair cells in the GER in all three conditions took up the FM 1–43 dye within 10 s (Figure 2B), although the degree of labeling of the reprogrammed cells in the GER was significantly fainter than the endogenous hair cells visible in the organ of Corti.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by FM1-43 dye uptake assay data.

claim: Cell proliferation occurred only in the spiral ganglion region and not in the organ of Corti of experimental or control animals.
source: We observed that cell proliferation occurred only in the spiral ganglion region and not in the organ of Corti of experimental or control animals, and none of the reprogrammed hair cells in the GER were labeled by EdU (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by EdU incorporation assay data.

claim: None of the reprogrammed hair cells in the GER were labeled by EdU.
source: We observed that cell proliferation occurred only in the spiral ganglion region and not in the organ of Corti of experimental or control animals, and none of the reprogrammed hair cells in the GER were labeled by EdU (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by EdU incorporation assay data.

claim: The vast majority of reprogrammed hair cells in the GER are generated by direct non-mitotic reprogramming, rather than by proliferation.
source: These data suggest that the vast majority of the reprogrammed hair cells we observe in the GER are generated by direct non-mitotic reprogramming, rather than by proliferation.
evidence: This is an inference from the EdU incorporation data.

claim: Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis was performed on reprogrammed cells purified by FACS at P8.
source: These mice were injected with tamoxifen at P1 and tdTomato-positive cochlear cells were purified by FACS at P8 (Figure 3A) and used to generate scRNA-seq libraries using the 10xGenomics Chromium platform.
evidence: This describes the methodology used in the study.

claim: Cell clustering after integration of cells from all four genotypes allowed identification of expected cell-type-specific clusters.
source: The cell clustering pattern observed after the integration of cells from all four genotypes allowed us to identify expected cell-type-specific clusters based on transcriptomic data from previous studies (Kolla et al., 2020).
evidence: This describes the analysis approach and results, supported by scRNA-seq data and citation.

claim: Sensory and non-sensory cells of the cochlear duct were identified in the clustering, including hair cells, supporting cells, greater epithelial ridge cells, cells of the stria vascularis, and glial cells.
source: Sensory and non-sensory cells of the cochlear duct, including hair cells, supporting cells, greater epithelial ridge cells, cells of the stria vascularis, and glial cells were all identified in the clustering (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Reprogrammed hair cells expressed significant levels of genes associated with hair cell mechanotransduction (Tmc1, Tmie, Lhfpl5, Cdh23, Pcdh15) compared to GER or supporting cells.
source: Consistent with our successful FM1-43 labeling of the new hair cells, we observed significant expression of genes associated with hair cell mechanotransduction (Tmc1, Tmie, Lhfpl5, Cdh23, Pcdh15) compared to GER or supporting cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Clustering analysis confirmed a reduction in cells of the GER (particularly lateral GER) but a significant increase in the numbers of hair cells in the three reprogrammed conditions compared to control mice.
source: Our clustering analysis confirmed the results obtained by staining with cell-type-specific markers: we saw a reduction in cells of the GER (particularly lateral GER) but a significant increase in the numbers of hair cells in the three reprogrammed conditions compared to control mice (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Gene ontology analysis of reprogrammed hair cells identified top GO hits including genes for sensory perception of sound, inner ear morphogenesis, auditory receptor cell differentiation, cilium morphogenesis, and cell projection organization.
source: The top GO hits included genes for sensory perception of sound (GO: 0007605, 27 genes, p=1.40E–13), inner ear morphogenesis (GO: 0042472, 12 genes, p=5.70E–04), auditory receptor cell differentiation (GO: 0042491, 7 genes, p=5.70E–04), cilium morphogenesis (GO:0060271,17 genes, p=7.50E–04) and cell projection organization (GO:0030030,16 genes, p=7.50E–04; Figure 3E).
evidence: This is a finding from the gene ontology analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: Reprogrammed hair cells possess many morphological and transcriptional characteristics similar to endogenous inner hair cells.
source: Together, our data suggest that reprogrammed hair cells possess many morphological and transcriptional characteristics similar to endogenous inner hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from multiple lines of experimental data.

claim: At P8, the addition of Gfi1 and Pou4f3 does not improve the morphology of the reprogrammed hair cells, nor a more complete complement of hair cell genes expressed in the reprogrammed cells.
source: However, they also show that at this age, the addition of Gfi1 and Pou4f3 does not improve the morphology of the reprogrammed hair cells, nor a more complete complement of hair cell genes expressed in the reprogrammed cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq and morphological data.

claim: Between P7 and P15, parts of the GER undergo remodeling through thyroid-hormone-dependent apoptosis and are replaced by cuboidal inner sulcus cells.
source: Between P7 and P15, parts of the GER undergo remodeling through thyroid-hormone-dependent apoptosis and are replaced by cuboidal inner sulcus cells (Peeters et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: By P15, several rows of SOX9+ GER cells remain on the lateral edge of the inner sulcus adjacent to the organ of Corti.
source: By P15 several rows of SOX9 +GER cells remain on the lateral edge of the inner sulcus adjacent to the organ of Corti.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Rosa-GAP mice show approximately 50-60 ectopic hair cells per 200 µm at P15, whereas Rosa-A and Rosa-GA show less than 5 ectopic cells per 200 µm.
source: Rosa-GAP mice show approximately 50–60 ectopic hair cells, whereas Rosa-A and Rosa-GA show less than 5 ectopic cells per 200 µm.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Rosa26-GAP mice can reprogram GER cells to hair cell-like cells at P15.
source: Rosa26-GAP mice can reprogram GER cells to hair cell-like cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: New hair cells generated by Rosa-GAP mice at P15 were derived from Sox9-expressing supporting cells or GER cells.
source: By using an Ai9 Rosa-tdTomato reporter line, we demonstrated that these new hair cells were derived from Sox9-expressing supporting cells or GER cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by lineage tracing data.

claim: New hair cells generated by Rosa-GAP mice continued to survive until at least P29 and showed increasing organization of phalloidin-stained hair bundles with increasing age.
source: These new hair cells continued to survive until at least P29 and showed increasing organization of phalloidin-stained hair bundles with increasing age (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data over time.

claim: P15 reprogrammed hair cells in the Rosa26-GAP condition did not express the inner hair cell marker VGLUT3.
source: Immunostaining of the reprogrammed cells revealed that, unlike the younger reprogrammed cells, P15 reprogrammed hair cells in the Rosa26-GAP condition did not express the inner hair cell marker VGLUT3 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: P15 reprogrammed hair cells showed evidence of innervation based on staining with TuJ1 antibody.
source: These reprogrammed hair cells did, however, show evidence of innervation based on staining with TuJ1 antibody, and formed ribbon synapses based on positive staining for CTBP2 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: P15 reprogrammed hair cells formed ribbon synapses based on positive staining for CTBP2.
source: These reprogrammed hair cells did, however, show evidence of innervation based on staining with TuJ1 antibody, and formed ribbon synapses based on positive staining for CTBP2 (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Individual hair cell stereocilia of reprogrammed hair cells at P15 were immature compared to endogenous hair cells and P8 reprogrammed hair cells.
source: Higher magnification SEM images at 50,000 X revealed that individual hair cell stereocilia of reprogrammed hair cells in all three conditions were immature compared to endogenous hair cells and the P1 reprogrammed hair cells we observed at P8.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by scanning electron microscopy data.

claim: Many of the ectopic cells at P15 possessed kinocilia but the stereocilia did not exhibit a staircase-like structure and still contained many side links between individual stereocilia, indicating their immature state.
source: Many of the ectopic cells possessed kinocilia but the stereocilia did not exhibit a staircase-like structure and still contained many side links between individual stereocilia, indicating their immature state (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by scanning electron microscopy data.

claim: Some of the ectopic hair cells produced in all three conditions at P15 were able to take up the dye FM1-43X, suggesting rudimentary mechanotransduction activity.
source: Some of the ectopic hair cells produced in all three conditions were able to take up the dye FM1-43X, suggesting that at least some of the cells have some rudimentary mechanotransduction activity (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by FM1-43X dye uptake assay data.

claim: All three overexpression conditions are capable of producing reprogrammed hair-cell-like cells at P15, but the Rosa26-GAP cocktail is significantly more efficient.
source: Together, we established that all three overexpression conditions are capable of producing reprogrammed hair-cell-like cells at P15, but the Rosa26-GAP cocktail is significantly more efficient at producing new hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the quantitative and qualitative data.

claim: Reprogrammed hair cells created between P8 and P15 are less mature than those derived from reprogramming neonatal cells between P1 and P8.
source: Nevertheless, these reprogrammed hair cells created between P8 and P15 are less mature than those derived from reprogramming neonatal cells between P1 and P8.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from comparing the morphological and functional data at different ages.

claim: Reprogrammed hair cells at P15 expressed some genes coding for proteins of the mechanotransduction apparatus (Tmie, Lhfpl5, Pcdh15).
source: The reprogrammed hair cells also expressed some genes coding for proteins of the mechanotransduction apparatus (Tmie, Lhfpl5, Pcdh15; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), although the range of mechanotransduction genes was less than in reprogrammed hair cells in P8 mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: The range of mechanotransduction genes expressed in P15 reprogrammed hair cells was less than in P8 reprogrammed hair cells.
source: The reprogrammed hair cells also expressed some genes coding for proteins of the mechanotransduction apparatus (Tmie, Lhfpl5, Pcdh15; Figure 6—figure supplement 1B), although the range of mechanotransduction genes was less than in reprogrammed hair cells in P8 mice (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis comparing P8 and P15 data.

claim: Neither Tmc1 nor Tmc2 channels were detected at significant levels in P15 reprogrammed hair cells.
source: We were not able to detect significant levels of either the Tmc1 or Tmc2 channels at this age, consistent with the low amount of FM1-43X labeling in the ectopic hair cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis, consistent with the FM1-43X data.

claim: Hair cells obtained from all three overexpression conditions at P15 are transcriptionally similar and possess immature hair cell-like features.
source: Taken together, we have shown that hair cells obtained from all three overexpression conditions are transcriptionally similar and possess immature hair cell-like features.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq and morphological data.

claim: The Rosa26-GAP reprogramming mice generate more hair cells at P15, but their transcriptional profile did not differ significantly from hair cells observed in Rosa-A or Rosa-GA conditions.
source: However, although the Rosa26-GAP reprogramming mice generate more hair cells, their transcriptional profile did not differ significantly from hair cells observed in Rosa-A or Rosa-GA conditions, suggesting that the additional reprogramming factors increase the efficiency, but not the fidelity of hair cell reprogramming.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the scRNA-seq data.

claim: The additional reprogramming factors (GFI1, POU4F3) increase the efficiency, but not the fidelity of hair cell reprogramming at P15.
source: However, although the Rosa26-GAP reprogramming mice generate more hair cells, their transcriptional profile did not differ significantly from hair cells observed in Rosa-A or Rosa-GA conditions, suggesting that the additional reprogramming factors increase the efficiency, but not the fidelity of hair cell reprogramming.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the scRNA-seq data.

claim: Some supporting cells of the organ of Corti (Deiters' cells and pillar cells) did not respond to the reprogramming factors by expressing hair cell proteins or exhibiting morphological changes.
source: A consistent observation in our reprogramming experiments conducted between P1-P8 and P8-P15 was that some supporting cells of the organ of Corti – the Deiters' cells and pillar cells – did not respond to the reprogramming factors by expressing hair cell proteins such as Myosin VIIA and did not exhibit any morphological changes indicating they were transforming into hair cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Under all three reprogramming conditions at both P1-P8 and P8-P15, there was no conversion of Deiters' cells or pillar cells into Myosin VIIA+ hair cells.
source: Under all three reprogramming conditions at both stages (P1-P8 and P8-P15), we consistently failed to see conversion of Deiters' cells or pillar cells into Myosin VIIA + hair cells (Figure 7—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Signals from hair cells, particularly the Notch signaling pathway, are known to promote and stabilize supporting cell fate during development.
source: Signals from hair cells, particularly the Notch signaling pathway, are known to promote and stabilize supporting cell fate during development (Basch et al., 2016b; Woods et al., 2004) and induce supporting cell fate in the presence of ectopic hair cells (Kelly et al., 2012; Woods et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Notch signaling can induce supporting cell fate in the presence of ectopic hair cells.
source: Signals from hair cells, particularly the Notch signaling pathway, are known to promote and stabilize supporting cell fate during development (Basch et al., 2016b; Woods et al., 2004) and induce supporting cell fate in the presence of ectopic hair cells (Kelly et al., 2012; Woods et al., 2004).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Cells in the reprogrammed GER lying beneath the reprogrammed Myosin VIIA+ hair cells expressed GLAST and SOX2 protein, but not PROX1.
source: We found that cells in the reprogrammed GER lying beneath the reprogrammed Myosin VIIA+hair cells expressed GLAST and SOX2 protein, but not PROX1 (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: The reprogrammed hair cells were able to promote the formation of inner phalangeal cell and border cell-like cells from the GER.
source: This suggested the reprogrammed hair cells were able to promote the formation of inner phalangeal cell and border cell-like cells from the GER, even though these cells were also expressing the reprogramming factor combinations.
evidence: This is an inference from the immunostaining data showing GLAST and SOX2 expression.

claim: Approximately equal numbers of supporting cells were observed in the presence of all three transcription factor combinations.
source: We observed approximately equal numbers of supporting cells in the presence of all three transcription factor combinations, suggesting that even the presence of ATOH1, GFI1, and POU4F3 in GER cells was not sufficient to prevent them from forming supporting cell-like cells when apposed to reprogrammed hair cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by quantitative data.

claim: Even the presence of ATOH1, GFI1, and POU4F3 in GER cells was not sufficient to prevent them from forming supporting cell-like cells when apposed to reprogrammed hair cells.
source: We observed approximately equal numbers of supporting cells in the presence of all three transcription factor combinations, suggesting that even the presence of ATOH1, GFI1, and POU4F3 in GER cells was not sufficient to prevent them from forming supporting cell-like cells when apposed to reprogrammed hair cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the quantitative and immunostaining data.

claim: Cryab, Ccnd1, Rcn1, and Hes5 were upregulated in reprogrammed GLAST+ supporting cells in all three conditions.
source: Cryab, Ccnd1, Rcn1, and Hes5 were upregulated in all three cases.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: Hes5 expression in the reprogrammed GLAST positive cells is likely a response to active Notch signaling induced by the ectopic hair cells to maintain supporting cell identity.
source: Its expression in the reprogrammed GLAST positive cells is likely a response to active Notch signaling induced by the ectopic hair cells to maintain supporting cell identity (Wang et al., 2010).
evidence: This is an inference from the gene expression data, supported by a citation.

claim: Notch-receiving genes (Lfng, Notch1, and Hes1) were upregulated in the reprogrammed supporting cells at P8.
source: We observed the upregulation of Notch-receiving genes (Lfng, Notch1, and Hes1) in the reprogrammed supporting cells and hair cell-specific (Dll3, Jag2, and Dlk2) Notch ligand genes in the reprogrammed hair cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: Hair cell-specific Notch ligand genes (Dll3, Jag2, and Dlk2) were upregulated in the reprogrammed hair cells at P8.
source: We observed the upregulation of Notch-receiving genes (Lfng, Notch1, and Hes1) in the reprogrammed supporting cells and hair cell-specific (Dll3, Jag2, and Dlk2) Notch ligand genes in the reprogrammed hair cells (Figure 7C).
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: Transcription factor reprogramming is capable of reconstituting the Notch signaling interactions between hair cells and supporting cells.
source: This suggests that transcription factor reprogramming is capable of reconstituting the Notch signaling interactions between hair cells and supporting cells, and that these interactions are sufficient to repress the action of the three reprogramming transcription factors in the ectopically induced supporting cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the gene expression data showing Notch pathway activation.

claim: Notch signaling interactions between reprogrammed hair cells and supporting cells are sufficient to repress the action of the three reprogramming transcription factors in the ectopically induced supporting cells.
source: This suggests that transcription factor reprogramming is capable of reconstituting the Notch signaling interactions between hair cells and supporting cells, and that these interactions are sufficient to repress the action of the three reprogramming transcription factors in the ectopically induced supporting cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the gene expression data showing Notch pathway activation.

claim: Ectopic GLAST+, SOX2+ supporting cell-like cells were observed adjacent to reprogrammed hair cells in the Rosa26-GAP condition at P15.
source: We saw evidence for the presence of ectopic GLAST+, SOX2+supporting cell-like cells adjacent to reprogrammed hair cells in the Rosa26-GAP condition alone (Figure 8A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: None of the reprogrammed hair cells or supporting cells at P15 were generated by proliferation.
source: EdU injections given every second day from P8 to P15 showed that none of the reprogrammed hair cells or supporting cells were generated by proliferation. (Figure 8—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by EdU incorporation assay data.

claim: Notch pathway-associated genes like Mfng, Ccnd1, Hes5, and Dlk2 were upregulated in P15 supporting cells in response to transcription factor cocktails.
source: The most significant up and down-regulated genes are highlighted (Figure 8B), and include Notch pathway-associated genes like Mfng, Ccnd1, Hes5, and Dlk2.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: Many supporting cell genes such as Ttll3, Rorb, Scd1, Scnn1b, Hhatl, Washc2, and Caecam16 were downregulated in P15 supporting cells in response to transcription factor cocktails.
source: In parallel to this, we also observed downregulation of many supporting cell genes such as Ttll3, Rorb, Scd1, Scnn1b, Hhatl, Washc2 in addition to Caecam16.
evidence: This is a finding from the differential gene expression analysis of scRNA-seq data.

claim: 972 distal regulatory elements associated with hair cell genes were significantly more accessible in GER cells, inner phalangeal cells, and border cells at day 1 compared to day 8.
source: However, 972 elements were significantly more accessible in the three cell populations at day 1 compared to day 8.
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-omic analysis comparing P1 and P8 data.

claim: 498 distal regulatory elements associated with hair cell genes showed comparable accessibility in GER cells, inner phalangeal cells, and border cells at both day 1 and day 8.
source: 498 elements showed comparable accessibility in these cell populations at both ages.
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-omic analysis comparing P1 and P8 data.

claim: Hes6, Myo3b, and Pou4f3 loci all showed reduced accessibility at day 8 in distal or intergenic regulatory elements.
source: Hes6, Myo3b, and Pou4f3 all showed reduced accessibility at day 8 in distal or intergenic regulatory elements at older ages.
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-omic analysis, supported by ATAC-seq data.

claim: At P1, the Pou4f3 locus is epigenetically accessible in cells of the GER.
source: At P1, our multi-omic analysis shows that the Pou4f3 locus is epigenetically accessible in cells of the GER.
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-omic analysis, supported by ATAC-seq data.

claim: Accessible peaks with ATOH1 binding sites were identified in the Pou4f3 locus at P1.
source: We could identify accessible peaks with ATOH1 binding sites in this locus (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, C), suggesting that activation of ATOH1 in the GER at this age could also induce expression of POU4F3.
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-omic analysis, supported by ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN data.

claim: Activation of ATOH1 in the GER at P1 could induce expression of POU4F3.
source: We could identify accessible peaks with ATOH1 binding sites in this locus (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B, C), suggesting that activation of ATOH1 in the GER at this age could also induce expression of POU4F3.
evidence: This is an inference from the ATAC-seq and CUT&RUN data.

claim: Expression of ATOH1 alone induced POU4F3 protein throughout the GER within 3 days after tamoxifen addition at P1.
source: Accordingly, we found that expression of ATOH1 alone induced POU4F3 protein throughout the GER with 3 days after tamoxifen addition (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: In 8-day-old mice, the Pou4f3 locus was significantly less accessible in GER cells.
source: However, in 8-day-old mice, the Pou4f3 locus was significantly less accessible in GER cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that ATOH1 alone would not be sufficient to activate these factors in GER cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-omic analysis, supported by ATAC-seq data.

claim: ATOH1 alone would not be sufficient to activate POU4F3 in GER cells at P8.
source: However, in 8-day-old mice, the Pou4f3 locus was significantly less accessible in GER cells (Figure 9—figure supplement 1B), suggesting that ATOH1 alone would not be sufficient to activate these factors in GER cells.
evidence: This is an inference from the ATAC-seq data showing reduced accessibility.

claim: No evidence for induction of POU4F3 protein was seen when ATOH1 was activated in Rosa-A mice at P8 and analyzed at P11.
source: As expected, we saw no evidence for induction of POU4F3 protein when ATOH1 was activated in Rosa-A mice at P8 and POU4F3 analyzed by immunostaining at P11 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Co-expression of GFI1 and POU4F3 with ATOH1 in the 8-day-old cochlea can increase the efficiency of hair cell reprogramming.
source: Here, we show that the co-expression of ATOH1 with two other hair cell transcription factors, GFI1 and POU4F3, in Rosa-GAP mice can increase the efficiency of hair cell reprogramming in older animals compared to ATOH1 alone or GFI1 +ATOH1.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: The hair cells generated by reprogramming at 8 days of age with three hair cell transcription factors are significantly less mature than those generated by reprogramming at postnatal day 1.
source: However, the hair cells generated by reprogramming at 8 days of age – even with three hair cell transcription factors – are significantly less mature than those generated by reprogramming at postnatal day 1.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by morphological and functional data.

claim: Reprogramming with multiple transcription factors is better able to access the hair cell differentiation gene regulatory network.
source: By analyzing the epigenetic landscape of the cochlea over the first two postnatal weeks, we suggest that reprogramming with multiple transcription factors is better able to access the hair cell differentiation gene regulatory network, but that additional interventions may be necessary to produce mature and fully functional hair cells.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the multi-omic analysis and reprogramming experiments.

claim: Additional interventions may be necessary to produce mature and fully functional hair cells beyond using multiple transcription factors.
source: By analyzing the epigenetic landscape of the cochlea over the first two postnatal weeks, we suggest that reprogramming with multiple transcription factors is better able to access the hair cell differentiation gene regulatory network, but that additional interventions may be necessary to produce mature and fully functional hair cells.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on the study findings.

claim: The Gfi1 and Pou4f3 genes are direct transcriptional targets of ATOH1.
source: The simplest explanation for these results is that the Gfi1 and Pou4f3 genes are direct transcriptional targets of ATOH1 (Hertzano et al., 2004; Ikeda et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2021), and thus activation of either ATOH1 alone (or GFI1+ATOH1) would result in the activation of all three transcription factors, together with other transcriptional effectors of the hair cell gene regulatory network.
evidence: This is an inference supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Activation of ATOH1 alone (or GFI1+ATOH1) in neonatal mice would result in the activation of all three transcription factors (ATOH1, GFI1, POU4F3).
source: The simplest explanation for these results is that the Gfi1 and Pou4f3 genes are direct transcriptional targets of ATOH1 (Hertzano et al., 2004; Ikeda et al., 2015; Yu et al., 2021), and thus activation of either ATOH1 alone (or GFI1+ATOH1) would result in the activation of all three transcription factors, together with other transcriptional effectors of the hair cell gene regulatory network.
evidence: This is an inference from the experimental data and prior knowledge.

claim: Components of the hair cell gene regulatory network become refractory to induction by ATOH1 alone in older animals.
source: In contrast, activation of ATOH1 alone just one week later in P8 Rosa-A mice is unable to activate POU4F3 expression (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A) suggesting that components of the hair cell gene regulatory network – even those immediately downstream of Atoh1 – become refractory to induction by ATOH1 alone in older animals.
evidence: This is an inference from the immunostaining data showing lack of POU4F3 induction.

claim: The GER is undergoing significant apoptotic remodeling between P8 and P15 in response to thyroid hormone.
source: It is important to note that the GER is undergoing significant apoptotic remodeling at this time in response to thyroid hormone (Peeters et al., 2015), as shown by the loss of Sox9 lineage-labeled cells from the cochlea between P8 and P15 (Figure S4A).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation and lineage tracing data.

claim: GER remodeling likely leads to a loss of cells capable of being reprogrammed by Rosa-GAP mice, leading to an under-estimate of reprogramming capability.
source: This remodeling likely leads to a loss of cells capable of being reprogrammed by Rosa-GAP mice, which we suggest leads to an under-estimate of the reprogramming capability of Rosa-GAP mice in these experiments.
evidence: This is an inference from the GER remodeling data.

claim: Myosin VIIa+ cells produced by Rosa-GAP mice at P15 do not have organized actin bundles on their apical surface that can be labeled by phalloidin initially.
source: Consistent with this possibility, we note that Myosin VIIa + cells produced by Rosa-GAP mice at P15 do not have organized actin bundles on their apical surface that can be labeled by phalloidin.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: Organized actin bundles begin to appear on GAP-reprogrammed hair cells over the two weeks following P15.
source: Significantly, such bundles begin to appear on these GAP-reprogrammed hair cells over the following two weeks, but not in the small number of extra hair cells generated by Rosa-A mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by immunostaining data over time.

claim: Persistent expression of ATOH1 may militate against full maturation of the new hair cells generated in reprogramming studies.
source: It is also important to note that our current over-expression model causes continued expression of ATOH1 in our reprogrammed cells, whereas Atoh1 expression is normally downregulated in hair cells shortly after they begin to differentiate. Such persistent expression may militate against full maturation of the new hair cells generated in our studies, and in previous studies that have used constitutive activation of Atoh1 as a reprogramming strategy (Chen et al., 2021; Kelly et al., 2012; Lee et al., 2020; Liu et al., 2012; Menendez et al., 2020; Walters et al., 2017; Yamashita et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative inference about the limitations of the experimental approach.

claim: Developmental signals that may specify inner versus outer hair cells may have disappeared by P15.
source: However, we saw no evidence for this in our P15 reprogrammed cells, suggesting that developmental signals that may specify inner versus outer hair cells may have disappeared by this age.
evidence: This is an inference from the lack of VGLUT3 expression in P15 reprogrammed cells.

claim: Reprogramming with additional transcription factors specific for hair cell sub-types may be necessary to generate specific kinds of hair cells in older animals.
source: Reprogramming with additional transcription factors specific for hair cell sub-types – such as Ikzf2 or Insm1 for outer hair cells (Chessum et al., 2018; Wiwatpanit et al., 2018) or Tbx2 for inner hair cells (García-Añoveros et al., 2022) may be necessary to generate specific kinds of hair cells in older animals.
evidence: This is a speculative suggestion based on the study findings and prior research.

claim: Atoh1 and Ikzf2 can co-operate to produce hair cells with some properties of outer hair cells.
source: Indeed, a recent report suggests that Atoh1 and Ikzf2 can co-operate to produce hair cells with some properties of outer hair cells (Sun et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Supporting cells are essential for the function and survival of inner ear hair cells.
source: Supporting cells are essential for the function and survival of inner ear hair cells.
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field.

claim: During development, hair cells and supporting cells derive from a common progenitor.
source: During development, hair cells and supporting cells derive from a common progenitor, and the correct proportion of these two cell types is regulated by several signaling pathways, most prominently Notch signaling (reviewed by Basch et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: The correct proportion of hair cells and supporting cells is regulated by several signaling pathways, most prominently Notch signaling.
source: During development, hair cells and supporting cells derive from a common progenitor, and the correct proportion of these two cell types is regulated by several signaling pathways, most prominently Notch signaling (reviewed by Basch et al., 2016a).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by a citation.

claim: Interventions that promote conversion of supporting cells into hair cells without replacing the original supporting cells are unlikely to lead to the restoration of a functional organ of Corti.
source: Interventions that promote conversion of supporting cells into hair cells without replacing the original supporting cells are unlikely to lead to the restoration of a functional organ of Corti.
evidence: This is a logical inference based on the essential role of supporting cells.

claim: Non-mammalian vertebrates accomplish hair cell regeneration by triggering transient proliferation of at least some supporting cells during the regenerative process.
source: Non-mammalian vertebrates accomplish this by triggering transient proliferation of at least some supporting cells during the regenerative process, and such transient proliferation may be important to promote functional hair cell regeneration in mammals.
evidence: This is established knowledge about non-mammalian vertebrate regeneration.

claim: Transient proliferation of supporting cells may be important to promote functional hair cell regeneration in mammals.
source: Non-mammalian vertebrates accomplish this by triggering transient proliferation of at least some supporting cells during the regenerative process, and such transient proliferation may be important to promote functional hair cell regeneration in mammals.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on non-mammalian vertebrate regeneration.

claim: The generation of reprogrammed hair cells can generate new supporting cells in the surrounding tissue through non-cell-autonomous mechanisms, including Notch signaling.
source: However, the generation of reprogrammed hair cells can generate new supporting cells in the surrounding tissue through non-cell-autonomous mechanisms, again including Notch signaling (Stone and Cotanche, 1994; Wan et al., 2020; Zhang et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The production of large numbers of reprogrammed hair cell-like cells in the GER causes the induction of GLAST+ supporting cells that interleave the new hair cells.
source: In the present study, we have shown that the production of large numbers of reprogrammed hair cell-like cells in the GER causes the induction of GLAST + supporting cells that interleave the new hair cells.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by immunostaining data.

claim: The identity of ectopic supporting cells in the reprogrammed GER resembles border cells and inner phalangeal cells.
source: Of note, the new hair cells produced in the GER resemble inner ear hair cells, and our scRNA-seq and antibody characterization shows that the identity of ectopic supporting cells resembles border cells and inner phalangeal cells, two supporting cell types that normally surround inner hair cells.
evidence: This is a finding from the study, supported by scRNA-seq and immunostaining data.

claim: Reprogramming in the GER is able to generate appropriately patterned and location-specific mosaics of hair cells and supporting cells similar to those that occur in vivo.
source: Reprogramming in the GER is, therefore, able to generate appropriately patterned and location-specific mosaics of hair cells and supporting cells similar to those that occur in vivo.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the characterization of reprogrammed cells.

claim: The new supporting cell-like cells retain their identity despite continuing to express hair cell reprogramming factors, suggesting that signaling pathways can override the action of the reprogramming factors.
source: The fact that the new supporting cell-like cells retain their identity despite continuing to express hair cell reprogramming factors suggests that signaling pathways present in supporting cells can override the action of the reprogramming factors.
evidence: This is an inference from the observation that supporting cells form despite expressing reprogramming factors.

claim: Most organ of Corti supporting cells in neonatal mice rapidly and readily trans-differentiate into hair cells when Notch signaling is blocked.
source: First, most organ of Corti supporting cells in neonatal mice rapidly and readily trans-differentiate into hair cells when Notch signaling is blocked (Jiang et al., 2014; Korrapati et al., 2013; Mizutari et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Blocking Notch signaling with gamma-secretase inhibitors can cause ectopic supporting cells in the GER created by ATOH1 reprogramming to transdifferentiate to hair cells.
source: Second, blocking Notch signaling with gamma-secretase inhibitors can cause ectopic supporting cells in the GER created by ATOH1 reprogramming to transdifferentiate to hair cells (Kelly et al., 2012).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior research.

claim: Elements of the Notch signaling pathway are reconstituted in the ectopic supporting cells generated in reprogrammed mice.
source: Third, our scRNA-seq data suggests that elements of the Notch signaling pathway are reconstituted in the ectopic supporting cells generated in our mice (Figure 7), and in endogenous supporting cells that receive reprogramming factors from P8-P15 (Figure 8).
evidence: This is a finding from the scRNA-seq analysis.

claim: Supporting cells normally transcriptionally and epigenetically down-regulate the Notch pathway in the first postnatal week and become refractory to Notch inhibition.
source: This latter result is particularly notable, as supporting cells normally transcriptionally and epigenetically down-regulate the Notch pathway in the first postnatal week and become refractory to Notch inhibition (Maass et al., 2015; Maass et al., 2016; Tao et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Transcription factor reprogramming may reconstitute some of the transcriptional and epigenetic regulation that normally exists between developing hair cells and supporting cells.
source: Together, our data suggest that transcription factor reprogramming may reconstitute some of the transcriptional and epigenetic regulation that normally exists between developing hair cells and supporting cells, and it will be of interest in the future to understand how fully these regulatory circuits can be established by different combinations of transcription factors.
evidence: This is an inference from the gene expression data showing Notch pathway reconstitution.

claim: The chromatin of hair cell loci becomes less accessible in supporting cells and GER cells during the first postnatal week.
source: In addition to the effects of Notch signaling, our multi-omic analysis of cochlear tissue at P1 and P8 shows clearly that the chromatin of hair cell loci becomes less accessible in supporting cells and GER cells during the first postnatal week (Figure 9).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the multi-omic analysis.

claim: The decrease in chromatin accessibility affects hair cell loci in general, including key hair cell transcription factors downstream of Atoh1 such as Gfi1 and Pou4f3.
source: This decrease in accessibility affects hair cell loci in general, but significantly is also seen in key hair cell transcription factors downstream of Atoh1, including Gfi1 and Pou4f3 (Figure 9—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from the multi-omic analysis.

claim: The decrease in chromatin accessibility is a second element contributing to the need for multiple transcription factors to reprogram more mature cochlear tissue.
source: We suggest that this decrease in accessibility is a second element contributing to the need for multiple transcription factors to reprogram more mature cochlear tissue.
evidence: This is an inference from the multi-omic data.

claim: Overexpression of multiple hair cell transcription factors in the cochlea promotes more efficient reprogramming in older animals.
source: In conclusion, our work shows that while overexpression of multiple hair cell transcription factors in the cochlea clearly promotes more efficient reprogramming in older animals, significant challenges to producing viable, functional hair cells still remain.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, supported by experimental data.

claim: Significant challenges to producing viable, functional hair cells still remain despite using multiple transcription factors.
source: In conclusion, our work shows that while overexpression of multiple hair cell transcription factors in the cochlea clearly promotes more efficient reprogramming in older animals, significant challenges to producing viable, functional hair cells still remain.
evidence: This is a primary conclusion of the study, based on the maturity and functionality of reprogrammed cells.

claim: Future work will be necessary to determine whether more functional hair cells can be generated with extra hair cell transcription factors, by epigenetic modulation of hair cell loci in supporting cells, or by actively targeting the down-regulation of supporting cell genes during reprogramming.
source: Future work will be necessary to determine whether more functional hair cells can be generated with extra hair cell transcription factors, by epigenetic modulation of hair cell loci in supporting cells, or by actively targeting the down-regulation of supporting cell genes during reprogramming.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future research directions.

claim: The present work focuses exclusively on the intact organ of Corti.
source: Finally, we emphasize that our present work focuses exclusively on the intact organ of Corti.
evidence: This describes the scope of the current study.

claim: It is currently unknown what effect the acute and long-term pathological consequences of hair cell loss in the cochlea will have on the efficiency and fidelity of hair cell reprogramming.
source: We currently do not know what effect the acute and long-term pathological consequences of hair cell loss in the cochlea will have on the efficiency and fidelity of hair cell reprogramming, and addressing this question will be critical to promoting functional hair cell regeneration in the mammalian cochlea.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study and future research needs.
